claims.text: EAM reference models are configurationally inadequate for high-entropy alloys near their melting temperatures.
Replacing EAM references with MLIPs trained on ab initio liquid configurations will overcome this configurational inadequacy.
The proposed MLIP would be trained on diverse ab initio liquid and solid configurations using active learning.
The trained MLIP would replace the EAM model as the thermodynamic-integration reference.
The method is applicable to HEAs containing 5–10 major component elements.
The method is applicable from just below to above the alloy melting point.
Liquids in this temperature range exhibit significant configurational diversity.
MLIPs capture a broader and more accurate distribution of atomic configurations than EAM references.
This broader configurational representation produces tighter phase-space overlap between the MLIP reference and the target ab initio liquid.
Training directly on ab initio data from solid and liquid phases enables MLIPs to reproduce the target energy landscape and atomic forces more accurately than empirical EAM references.
Improved reproduction of energies and forces reduces discrepancies along the thermodynamic-integration coupling path.
The MLIP reference is predicted to reduce TI path mismatch by roughly a factor of two relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The MLIP method is predicted to produce free energies in closer agreement with direct ab initio benchmarks than the EAM-based method.
TOR-TILD's EAM references inadequately span the configurational space of ab initio HEA liquids.
The method should be most effective for moderately compositionally complex HEAs when sufficient ab initio training data are available.
Performance outside the trained composition or temperature range is uncertain.
The estimated two-fold reduction in TI mismatch is based on trends from elemental and binary systems.
The extension of those elemental and binary trends to multicomponent HEAs has not yet been thoroughly tested.
